subject: radiology
title: SVC syndrome and venous recanalisation

steps.tx: Caval obstruction swells the face, because venous blood from head and arms cannot reach the heart normally. **SVC syndrome** balloons the face with neck vein distension and arm swelling that worsens when bending forward. **Malignant compression** from lung tumours and nodes drives most cases and often needs urgent stenting for relief. Benign fibrosing disease from chronic catheters suits gradual recanalisation rather than emergency stenting in stable patients. **Stridor with confusion** marks severe obstruction and needs emergency airway support alongside urgent stent treatment in hospital.
steps.say: Caval obstruction is dramatic because it swells the face when venous blood cannot reach the heart. Caval syndrome balloons the face with neck distension and arm swelling that worsens bending forward. Malignant compression from lung tumours and nodes drives most cases and needs urgent stenting. Benign scarring from chronic catheters suits gradual reopening rather than emergency stenting in stable patients. Stridor with confusion marks severe obstruction and needs emergency airway support alongside treatment.

steps.tx: Venous stenting reopens the caval highway quickly, and facial swelling often deflates on the same day. A **self expanding venous stent** scaffolds the cava and brachiocephalic trunks with strong radial support after deployment. **Through and through access** from groin and neck steadies crossing when the cava occludes completely in the chest. **Kissing stents** rebuild the bifurcation when both brachiocephalic veins fail together at the caval confluence. Anticoagulation after deployment keeps sluggish venous metal open and protects the reconstruction during early healing.

Anticoagulation after deployment keeps sluggish venous metal open and protects the reconstruction during healing.

steps.tx: These paired venograms compare caval obstruction before treatment with restored flow after stent deployment in the cava. The left panel shows a **high grade SVC obstruction** with tortuous mediastinal and azygos **collateral veins** that carry blood around the blockage. The right panel shows a **self expanding caval stent** that restores a straight channel toward the heart after deployment. The image matters for the exam because collateral burden proves severity while same day deflation proves stent success. Cause directed cancer treatment still continues because the stent bypasses rather than cures disease.

steps.tx: Leg swelling also follows venous compression, and iliac disease explains many unilateral presentations in clinic practice. **May Thurner compression** squeezes the left common iliac vein under the artery and breeds left leg clots with ulcers. **Iliac stenting** scaffolds that squeeze and gives lasting patency after clot clearance in the iliac segment. Dialysis outflow stenosis from old fistulae narrows central veins and needs balloons with selective stents for relief. **Post thrombotic scarring** can recanalise when organised clot still allows a wire to pass through the vein.
steps.say: Leg swelling also follows venous compression and iliac disease explains many unilateral presentations in clinic. Left iliac compression under the artery breeds left leg clots with ulcers over time. Iliac stenting scaffolds that squeeze and gives lasting patency after clot clearance in the segment. Dialysis outflow narrowing from old fistulae narrows central veins and needs balloon treatment for relief. Scarred veins after clot can reopen when organised clot still allows a wire through.

vis.caption: May-Thurner syndrome: Iliac vein compression treated with stenting

steps.tx: Follow up keeps venous metal moving, because slow venous flow restenoses faster than arterial flow after stenting. **Duplex with symptom checks** pairs velocity against swelling at every visit for that patient in clinic. Restenosis with a returning swollen face earns **re ballooning** before total re occlusion closes the cava again. **Stent position checks** confirm placement after coughing fits and trauma that could shift the scaffold slightly. Cause directed therapy for tumour and lines continues because a stent bypasses blockage rather than curing disease.
